correctness.rationale: For at most seven selected vertices, one or two points meet at most four or seven lines, forcing at least nine or six selected lines, and zero points forces all lines. Duality then leaves only (3,3), (3,4), (4,3). Three noncollinear points force four external lines; three collinear points force their common line and three external lines, all through the unselected fourth point, which violates the upper bound. For a triangle the external line forms (1,±1,±1) have no triple concurrence, cover exactly ten points, and meet outside points at most twice. Duality yields exactly the oval configurations, with external lines forced. The four extensions of the coordinate triangle to an oval and the four triangles per oval give 234 of each. For equal-type jumps, the external lines determine the point set as the complement of their union, and the point set in turn determines the lines; no same-side replacement is possible. A cross-type jump must be triangle inclusion, and its line exchange is with the unique oval tangent at the removed point. An independently written exact checker constructs Singer translates in PG(2,3), exhausts both classes of selected vertices through total size seven using mandatory line choices, compares literal one-token adjacency with inclusion, and computes every BFS profile. It finds precisely the two asserted families, 936 edges and the common profile (1,4,12,30,60,96,114,96,47,8); thus connectivity, radius and diameter all follow.
residual_risks: The metric certificate is exhaustive for the single fixed projective plane, not a theorem for higher orders.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The pertinent alias is the triangle–oval incidence graph, or the clique incidence expansion of the old oval graph, not the old graph itself. Four-cliques of oval exchanges are exactly the four extensions of a common triangle: a pairwise-three-overlap family of four 4-sets either shares a fixed triple or lies in a common 5-set; in the latter case any collinear triple would be contained in one of four distinct 4-subsets, and there is no 5-arc in PG(2,3). This makes the abstract mixed graph recoverable from old full adjacency, not an unrelated new graph. The independent optimizer identification is the main distinction.
